```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Education is a state, local, and family responsibility, not a federal obligation, under the American Constitutional system.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Over 90 percent of public school funding is state and local, not federal.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"State and local governments must assume most of the responsibility to improve schools.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The role of the federal government in education must be limited as control is returned to parents, teachers, and local school boards.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"President Bush and Congressional Republicans have provided the largest increase in federal education funding in history.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Federal education funding has had the highest percentage gain since the 1960s.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Support for elementary and secondary education has had the largest increase in any single Presidential term since the 1960s – an increase of nearly 50 percent since 2001.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The President and Congress are particularly focused on programs for America's neediest students, including minorities and children with special needs.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Increased funding for education comes with a new focus on achievement and results.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"High standards and accountability are priorities.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
